questions.stem: Four digit cards show 7, 0, 4 and 2. Lena uses all four cards, once each, to make the smallest four-digit number she can (a number may not begin with 0). Which number does she make?
questions.solution: The first digit must be as small as possible but not 0, so it is 2. Then the remaining cards go in increasing order: 0, 4, 7. The number is 2047.

solve.work: Smallest nonzero leading digit 2, then 0,4,7 ascending: 2047.

questions.stem: What is the last digit of the product $23 \times 47 \times 38$?
questions.solution: Only the last digits matter: $3 \times 7 = 21$ ends in 1, and $1 \times 8 = 8$. The product ends in 8.

questions.skill: order of operations with a negative
questions.stem: What is the value of $20 - 4 \times (7 - 9)$?
questions.solution: The bracket is $7 - 9 = -2$. Then $4 \times (-2) = -8$, and $20 - (-8) = 28$.

questions.stem: Which of these numbers is a prime number?
questions.solution: 57 = 3 x 19, 87 = 3 x 29 and 91 = 7 x 13 all have smaller factors. 61 has no divisor other than 1 and itself, so it is prime.

questions.stem: The sum of three consecutive whole numbers is 75. What is the largest of the three numbers?
questions.solution: The middle number is $75 \div 3 = 25$, so the numbers are 24, 25 and 26. The largest is 26.

questions.stem: Fatima writes the number made of 3 thousands, 14 hundreds and 7 tens. Which number is it?
questions.solution: 3 thousands is 3000, 14 hundreds is 1400 and 7 tens is 70. Together $3000 + 1400 + 70 = 4470$.

questions.stem: What is the value of $-6 - (-4) + 3$?
questions.solution: Subtracting $-4$ is the same as adding 4, so $-6 + 4 = -2$. Then $-2 + 3 = 1$.

questions.skill: largest number with given digit sum
questions.stem: What is the largest two-digit number whose two digits add up to 16?
questions.solution: Make the tens digit as large as possible: 9. Then the units digit must be $16 - 9 = 7$. The number is 97.

questions.stem: The two-digit number with tens digit 2 and units digit A is added to the two-digit number with tens digit A and units digit 2. The sum is 66. What digit is A?
questions.solution: The sum is $(20 + A) + (10A + 2) = 22 + 11A$. Setting this equal to 66 gives $11A = 44$, so $A = 4$ (check: $24 + 42 = 66$).

questions.stem: What is the value of $(8 + 4) \div 2 \times 3 - 5$?
questions.solution: Work left to right after the bracket: $12 \div 2 = 6$, then $6 \times 3 = 18$, then $18 - 5 = 13$.

questions.stem: How many two-digit numbers have digits whose product is 12?
questions.solution: The digit pairs with product 12 are 2 and 6, and 3 and 4 (1 and 12 is impossible). Each pair gives two numbers: 26, 62, 34 and 43. That is 4 numbers.

questions.stem: The six digit cards 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 are split into two groups of three, and each group is arranged into a three-digit number. What is the largest possible sum of the two numbers?
questions.solution: To make the sum large, the two hundreds digits should be 6 and 5, the tens digits 4 and 3, and the units digits 2 and 1. The sum is $11 \times 100 + 7 \times 10 + 3 = 1173$ however the cards are paired up.

questions.stem: A four-digit number has digits 3, A, 8, B in this order, where A and B are digits (A and B may be equal). It is divisible by both 5 and 9. How many such numbers are there?
questions.solution: Divisible by 5 means B is 0 or 5. If B = 0 the digit sum is $11 + A$, which is a multiple of 9 only for A = 7 (3780). If B = 5 the digit sum is $16 + A$, so A = 2 (3285). That gives 2 numbers.

questions.stem: The sum of five consecutive odd whole numbers is 135. What is the largest of them?
questions.solution: The middle number is $135 \div 5 = 27$. The numbers are 23, 25, 27, 29, 31, so the largest is 31.

questions.stem: With how many zeros does the number $15 \times 20 \times 35 \times 40$ end?
questions.solution: Each zero at the end needs a factor 2 and a factor 5. The factors 15, 20, 35 and 40 contain four 5s in total and at least five 2s, so there are 4 zeros (indeed the product is 420000).

questions.skill: negative numbers and order of operations
questions.stem: What is the value of $15 - 4 \times (3 - 8) \div (-2)$?
questions.solution: The bracket is $3 - 8 = -5$. Then $4 \times (-5) = -20$ and $-20 \div (-2) = 10$. Finally $15 - 10 = 5$.

questions.stem: In how many ways can 50 be written as the sum of two different prime numbers? (The order of the two primes does not matter.)
questions.solution: The pairs are 3 + 47, 7 + 43, 13 + 37 and 19 + 31. No other prime p below 25 has 50 - p prime (5, 11, 17, 23 give 45, 39, 33, 27; 2 gives 48). So there are 4 ways.

questions.stem: A and B are digits and A is not 0. The two-digit number with tens digit A and units digit B, multiplied by A, equals 96. What is $A + B$?
questions.solution: Try A = 3: the number is $30 + B$ and $3 \times (30 + B) = 96$ gives $B = 2$. A = 1 and A = 2 give products that are too small to fit (A = 2 would need $B = 28$), and A = 4 or more gives at least 160. So the number is 32 and $A + B = 5$.

questions.stem: All the whole numbers from 1 to 20 are written out in the usual way. What is the sum of all the digits that are written?
questions.solution: The numbers 1 to 9 give digit sum 45. The numbers 10 to 19 have ten tens digits equal to 1 (sum 10) and units digits 0 to 9 (sum 45), giving 55. The number 20 gives 2. In total $45 + 55 + 2 = 102$.

questions.stem: Four consecutive whole numbers (starting from 0 or higher) are added. Which of these numbers can NOT be the sum?
questions.solution: Four consecutive numbers $n, n+1, n+2, n+3$ add to $4n + 6$, which leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4. The numbers 38, 46 and 54 all leave remainder 2 (for example $8+9+10+11 = 38$), but 56 is a multiple of 4, so it cannot be such a sum.

questions.stem: Different letters stand for different digits, and no number begins with 0. The three two-digit numbers AB, BC and CA (for example, AB has tens digit A and units digit B) add up to the three-digit number ABC. What is ABC?
questions.solution: The sum of AB, BC and CA is $11(A + B + C)$, and it equals $100A + 10B + C$. So $89A = B + 10C$. Since B + 10C is at most 99, A = 1, giving $B + 10C = 89$, so C = 8 and B = 9. Check: $19 + 98 + 81 = 198$.

questions.skill: largest number with distinct digits and fixed digit sum
questions.stem: What is the largest whole number that has all its digits different and whose digits add up to 20?
questions.solution: Seven different digits add up to at least $0+1+\ldots+6 = 21$, so at most six digits are possible, and six is possible. For the largest number take the first digit 9; the other five different digits must add up to 11, and the only choice is 0, 1, 2, 3, 5. Arranged in decreasing order the number is 953210.

solve.work: 7 distinct digits sum at least 21, so 6 digits max; with 9 the rest sum 11: {0,1,2,3,5} only; 953210.

questions.skill: counting with divisibility and digit sum
questions.stem: How many three-digit numbers are divisible by 5 and have a digit sum of 12?
questions.solution: The number ends in 0 or 5. Ending in 0, the first two digits add to 12: (3,9), (4,8), (5,7), (6,6), (7,5), (8,4), (9,3), which is 7 numbers. Ending in 5, they add to 7: (1,6), (2,5), (3,4), (4,3), (5,2), (6,1), (7,0), also 7 numbers. In total 14.

questions.stem: The product of four consecutive positive whole numbers is 5040. What is the sum of the four numbers?
questions.solution: Four equal numbers near 8 would give $8^4 = 4096$, and near 9 would give $9^4 = 6561$, so the numbers are centred between 8 and 9. Try 7, 8, 9, 10: the product is $7 \times 8 \times 9 \times 10 = 5040$. Their sum is 34.

questions.stem: Two prime numbers add up to 2031. (It is known that 2029 is a prime number.) What is the product of the two primes?
questions.solution: 2031 is odd, so one of the two primes must be even, and the only even prime is 2. The other prime is $2031 - 2 = 2029$. The product is $2 \times 2029 = 4058$.

solve.work: Odd sum so one prime is 2, the other 2029; 2*2029=4058.

questions.stem: Three different numbers are chosen from the list $-7, -5, -2, 1, 3, 4$. What is the largest product they can have?
questions.solution: A positive product needs zero or two negative numbers. With two negatives, take the two with the largest size, $-7$ and $-5$, and the largest positive number 4: $(-7)(-5)(4) = 140$. With no negatives the best is $1 \times 3 \times 4 = 12$, and other choices such as $(-7)(-2)(4) = 56$ are smaller.

questions.skill: digit sum of a large number
questions.stem: Take the number made of a 1 followed by twelve zeros and subtract 2026 from it. What is the sum of the digits of the result?
questions.solution: The number $1000000000000 - 2026$ is 999999997974: since 10000 - 2026 = 7974, the last four digits are 7974, and the other eight digits are all 9. The digit sum is $8 \times 9 + 7 + 9 + 7 + 4 = 72 + 27 = 99$.

solve.work: 999999997974; or 12 nines (108) minus 2025 with no borrow: 108-9=99.

questions.stem: A three-digit number is equal to 31 times the sum of its digits. How many such numbers are there?
questions.solution: Write the number as $100a + 10b + c = 31(a + b + c)$, which gives $69a = 21b + 30c$, or $23a = 7b + 10c$. Trying a = 1 to 9, the solutions are 372, 465 and 558 (for example $31 \times 12 = 372$ and $3+7+2 = 12$). So there are 3.

questions.skill: square ending in its own digits
questions.stem: A two-digit number with tens digit A and units digit B is multiplied by itself. The result is the three-digit number with hundreds digit C, tens digit A and units digit B. (A, B and C are digits and A is not 0.) What is C?
questions.solution: If the number is n, then $n^2 = 100C + n$, so $n(n-1)$ must be a multiple of 100. The square has only three digits, so n is at most 31, and the only such n is 25, since $25 \times 24 = 600$. Indeed $25^2 = 625$, so C = 6.

solve.work: N^2 ends in N with N between 10 and 31: N=25, 625, C=6.

questions.skill: last digit of a long product
questions.stem: What is the last digit of the product $3 \times 13 \times 23 \times 33 \times \ldots \times 93$, whose ten factors all end in 3?
questions.solution: Only last digits matter, so we need the last digit of ten 3s multiplied together. The last digits go 3, 9, 7, 1 and then repeat every four factors. After ten factors we are at the same place as after two: 9.

solve.work: Last digit of 3^10; cycle 3,9,7,1, 10 mod 4=2 gives 9.

questions.stem: A choir has 60 singers, and 40% of them are boys. How many girls are in the choir?
questions.solution: 40% of 60 is 24 boys. So there are $60 - 24 = 36$ girls (that is 60% of 60).

questions.stem: Which of these four fractions is the greatest?
questions.solution: Over the common denominator 120 the fractions are 70/120, 72/120, 75/120 and 80/120. The greatest is 80/120, which is 2/3.

questions.stem: A bag holds 36 marbles. Half of them are red, and one third of the red marbles are large. How many large red marbles are there?
questions.solution: Half of 36 is 18 red marbles, and one third of 18 is 6.

questions.stem: A paint blend uses red and blue paint in the ratio 3 : 2 by volume. How many litres of blue paint go with 15 litres of red paint?
questions.solution: 15 litres is 3 parts, so one part is 5 litres. Blue is 2 parts, which is 10 litres.

questions.stem: A jacket costs 80 euros. In a sale, its price is reduced by 25%. What is the sale price in euros?
questions.solution: 25% of 80 is 20, so the sale price is $80 - 20 = 60$ euros.

questions.stem: What fraction of an hour is 18 minutes?
questions.solution: An hour has 60 minutes, so the fraction is $\frac{18}{60} = \frac{3}{10}$.

questions.stem: A book's price goes up from 50 euros to 65 euros. By what percentage of the old price has it increased?
questions.solution: The rise is $65 - 50 = 15$ euros. As a part of the old price, $\frac{15}{50} = 30\%$.

questions.stem: Anna and Ben share 45 stickers in the ratio 4 : 5. How many stickers does Ben get?
questions.solution: There are $4 + 5 = 9$ parts, so one part is 5 stickers. Ben gets 5 parts, which is 25 stickers.

questions.stem: Which fraction is equal to 0.35?
questions.solution: $0.35 = \frac{35}{100} = \frac{7}{20}$ after dividing top and bottom by 5.

questions.skill: finding the whole from a fraction
questions.stem: Three quarters of a number is 27. What is the number?
questions.solution: One quarter of the number is $27 \div 3 = 9$, so the whole number is $4 \times 9 = 36$.

questions.stem: A shop raises the price of a lamp by 25%. Later it lowers the new price by 20%. Compared with the original price, the final price is
questions.solution: Start with 100. After a 25% rise it is 125. A 20% cut of 125 removes 25, leaving 100, the same as at the start.

questions.stem: The length of a rectangle is increased by 20% and its width is decreased by 10%. What happens to its area?
questions.solution: The new area is $1.2 \times 0.9 = 1.08$ times the old area, so it increases by 8%.

questions.stem: Sam spends one third of his money on a book. He then spends one quarter of the money he has left on a snack. What fraction of his original money does he still have?
questions.solution: After the book, two thirds remain. One quarter of that is $\frac{1}{6}$ of the original, so what remains is $\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{2}$ (or $\frac{3}{4}$ of $\frac{2}{3}$).

questions.skill: ratio before and after a change
questions.stem: In a club the ratio of boys to girls is 3 : 5. After 8 more boys join, there are exactly as many boys as girls. How many girls are in the club?
questions.solution: Boys are $3k$ and girls $5k$ for some k. Then $3k + 8 = 5k$, so $k = 4$ and there are $5 \times 4 = 20$ girls.

questions.stem: There are 200 people at a fair, and 35% of them are children. Of the adults, 40% bought a ticket for the raffle. How many adults bought a ticket?
questions.solution: 35% of 200 is 70 children, so there are 130 adults. 40% of 130 is 52.

questions.stem: A painter mixes 3 litres of paint that is 20% blue pigment with 2 litres of paint that is 70% blue pigment. What percentage of the mixture is blue pigment?
questions.solution: The pigment is $0.2 \times 3 + 0.7 \times 2 = 0.6 + 1.4 = 2$ litres in 5 litres of paint, which is 40%.

questions.skill: fractions of a whole in steps
questions.stem: Mia reads one quarter of a book on Monday. On Tuesday she reads one third of the pages that were left after Monday. Now 60 pages are still unread. How many pages does the book have?
questions.solution: After Monday three quarters are left, and one third of that is one quarter of the whole book, which is read on Tuesday. So half the book has been read, and the 60 unread pages are the other half. The book has 120 pages.

questions.stem: Which of these fractions is closest to one half?
questions.solution: Their distances from one half are $\frac{1}{12}$, $\frac{1}{20}$, $\frac{1}{24}$ and $\frac{1}{30}$ respectively. The smallest distance is $\frac{1}{30}$, so the closest is $\frac{7}{15}$.

questions.stem: After a 20% discount, a bike costs 48 euros. What was its price before the discount, in euros?
questions.solution: The sale price is 80% of the old price, so the old price is $48 \div 0.8 = 60$ euros.

questions.stem: A shop takes 20% off a price and then takes 30% off the reduced price. Which single discount from the original price gives the same final price?
questions.solution: The final price is $0.8 \times 0.7 = 0.56$ of the original, so the single discount is $100\% - 56\% = 44\%$.

questions.skill: water content of fresh and dried fruit
questions.stem: Fresh apricots are 85% water by weight. Dried apricots are 25% water by weight. Only water is lost in drying. How many kilograms of fresh apricots are needed to make 6 kilograms of dried apricots?
questions.solution: Dried apricots are 75% solid, so 6 kg contain 4.5 kg of solid. Fresh apricots are 15% solid, and the solid is the same. So the fresh weight is $4.5 \div 0.15 = 30$ kg.

solve.work: Solids 6*0.75=4.5 kg = 15% of fresh, so 30 kg.

questions.stem: A share rises in value by 60% in its first year. In the second year its value falls by some percentage of its new value, so that after two years it is 20% above its starting value. By what percentage did it fall in the second year?
questions.solution: Start at 100. After the rise it is 160, and it ends at 120. The fall is 40, which is $\frac{40}{160} = 25\%$ of the value it had before falling.

questions.skill: ratio before and after a transfer
questions.stem: Ali and Bo have marbles in the ratio 7 : 5. Ali gives 10 of his marbles to Bo, and then the ratio of Ali's marbles to Bo's marbles is 3 : 5. How many marbles did Ali have at first?
questions.solution: Let Ali have $7k$ and Bo $5k$. Then $5(7k - 10) = 3(5k + 10)$, which gives $20k = 80$, so $k = 4$ and Ali had $7 \times 4 = 28$. Check: 18 and 30 are in ratio 3 : 5.

questions.stem: The ratio of Ana's money to Ben's money is 2 : 3, and the ratio of Ben's money to Chen's money is 4 : 5. Together they have 105 euros. How many more euros does Chen have than Ana?
questions.solution: Rewrite so that Ben has the same number of parts in both: Ana : Ben = 8 : 12 and Ben : Chen = 12 : 15. So Ana : Ben : Chen = 8 : 12 : 15, which is 35 parts. One part is $105 \div 35 = 3$ euros, and Chen has $15 - 8 = 7$ parts more than Ana, which is 21 euros.

questions.skill: adding pure substance to a mixture
questions.stem: A 10-litre mixture of juice and water is 40% juice. How many litres of pure juice must be added to make a mixture that is 60% juice?
questions.solution: The mixture has 4 litres of juice and 6 litres of water. The water stays the same and must become 40% of the new total, so the new total is $6 \div 0.4 = 15$ litres. So $15 - 10 = 5$ litres of juice are added.

solve.work: Water 6 L must be 40%: total 15, add 5.

questions.stem: In a class test, 60% of the pupils are girls. The girls' average mark is 80 and the boys' average mark is 65. What is the average mark of the whole class?
questions.solution: Take 10 pupils: 6 girls and 4 boys. The total of the marks is $6 \times 80 + 4 \times 65 = 480 + 260 = 740$, so the average is $740 \div 10 = 74$.

questions.stem: How many fractions with denominator 60 and a whole-number numerator lie strictly between $\frac{1}{5}$ and $\frac{1}{2}$ and cannot be simplified (are already in lowest terms)?
questions.solution: $\frac{1}{5} = \frac{12}{60}$ and $\frac{1}{2} = \frac{30}{60}$, so the numerator is from 13 to 29. A fraction over 60 is in lowest terms if the numerator has no factor 2, 3 or 5. These numerators are 13, 17, 19, 23 and 29, which is 5 fractions.

questions.stem: At a party 60% of the guests are adults. After 10 children leave, 75% of the guests who remain are adults. How many guests were at the party at first?
questions.solution: The number of adults does not change. If there were $N$ guests, adults are $0.6N$ and the remaining guests number $N - 10$, so $0.6N = 0.75(N - 10)$. This gives $0.15N = 7.5$, so $N = 50$. Check: 30 adults out of 40 is 75%.

questions.skill: rates as fractions of a tank
questions.stem: A tap alone fills an empty tank in 6 hours. A drain alone empties a full tank in 9 hours. The tank starts empty and the tap and the drain are opened together. How many hours does it take for the tank to be full?
questions.solution: Each hour the tap adds $\frac{1}{6}$ of the tank and the drain removes $\frac{1}{9}$, so the tank gains $\frac{1}{6} - \frac{1}{9} = \frac{1}{18}$ per hour. It is full after 18 hours.

questions.stem: All four fractions below are a little less than 1. Which of them lies closest to 1?
questions.solution: Each fraction is 1 minus a small gap: $\frac{3}{203}$, $\frac{2}{201}$, $\frac{1}{101}$ and $\frac{1}{102}$. The fraction closest to 1 has the smallest gap, and $\frac{1}{102}$ is the smallest of these gaps, so the closest is $\frac{101}{102}$.

questions.skill: sum and difference of two amounts
questions.stem: Kofi and Lena picked 29 apples together. Kofi picked 3 more apples than Lena. How many apples did Kofi pick?
questions.solution: If Lena had picked 3 more, both would have picked the same, and the total would be 32. So each would have 16, and that is what Kofi picked (Lena picked 13).

questions.stem: Dara thinks of a number, multiplies it by 3 and then adds 8. The result is 50. Which number did she think of?
questions.solution: Undo the steps in reverse order: 50 - 8 = 42, and 42 / 3 = 14.

questions.stem: Sam spent half of his money on a book and then 6 euros on lunch. Now he has 9 euros left. How many euros did Sam have at the start?
questions.solution: Before lunch he had 9 + 6 = 15 euros. That was the half left after the book, so he started with 2 x 15 = 30 euros.

questions.stem: Pia has 14 more stickers than Quinn. Pia gives some of her stickers to Quinn, and then they have the same number each. How many stickers does Pia give?
questions.solution: The gap of 14 must be closed from both sides. Each sticker given moves the gap by 2, so Pia gives 14 / 2 = 7 stickers.

solve.work: Half the difference of 14 is moved: 7.

questions.stem: At a fair, 5 adult tickets and 3 child tickets cost 39 euros in total. An adult ticket costs 6 euros. How many euros does one child ticket cost?
questions.solution: The adult tickets cost 5 x 6 = 30 euros. That leaves 39 - 30 = 9 euros for 3 child tickets, so one costs 3 euros.

questions.stem: Ten years ago Noor was 9 years old. Her sister is 4 years younger than Noor. How old will her sister be in 3 years' time?
questions.solution: Noor is now 9 + 10 = 19, so her sister is 15 now and will be 15 + 3 = 18 in 3 years.

questions.stem: Five numbers are written in a row. The first is 3, the second is 5, and every number after the second equals the sum of the two numbers just before it. What is the fifth number?
questions.solution: The row is 3, 5, 3 + 5 = 8, 5 + 8 = 13, 8 + 13 = 21. The fifth number is 21.

questions.stem: Four friends share a bill equally and each pays 12 euros. Then it turns out that one of them has left without paying, so the other three share the same bill equally. How many euros does each of the three pay?
questions.solution: The bill is 4 x 12 = 48 euros. Shared among three it is 48 / 3 = 16 euros each.

questions.stem: 9 identical notebooks cost 14 euros more than 5 of the same notebooks. How many euros does one notebook cost?
questions.solution: The extra 9 - 5 = 4 notebooks cost the extra 14 euros, so one notebook costs 14 / 4 = 3.5 euros.

questions.stem: Hugo already has 30 euros and saves 15 euros every month. After how many months will he have exactly 120 euros?
questions.solution: He still needs 120 - 30 = 90 euros, and 90 / 15 = 6 months.

questions.skill: the same quantity said in two ways
questions.stem: A jar full of honey weighs 900 g. When the jar is only $\frac{1}{3}$ full of honey, jar and honey together weigh 500 g. How many grams does the empty jar weigh?
questions.solution: Taking away $\frac{2}{3}$ of the honey lowers the weight from 900 g to 500 g, so $\frac{2}{3}$ of the honey weighs 400 g. All the honey weighs 600 g, and the empty jar weighs 900 - 600 = 300 g.

solve.work: 2/3 of the honey = 400 g, so honey 600 g, jar 300 g.

questions.stem: Zainab is 3 times as old as her son. In 12 years' time she will be twice as old as he is then. How old is her son now?
questions.solution: Let the son be x years old, so Zainab is 3x. In 12 years: 3x + 12 = 2(x + 12) = 2x + 24, which gives x = 12. (Check: 36 and 12 now, 48 and 24 later.)

questions.stem: Ada has 3 times as much money as Bo. Ada gives Bo 20 euros, and now Ada has exactly twice as much as Bo. How many euros did Ada have at first?
questions.solution: Let Bo have x euros, so Ada has 3x. Then 3x - 20 = 2(x + 20), so x = 60 and Ada had 3 x 60 = 180 euros. (Check: 160 and 80.)

questions.stem: Mr Wu sells half of his apples and 3 more in the morning. In the afternoon he sells half of the apples that are left and 2 more. After that 5 apples remain. How many apples did he have at the start?
questions.solution: Work backwards. Before the 2 extra apples he had 5 + 2 = 7, which was half of the afternoon's stock, so he had 14 after the morning. Then 14 + 3 = 17 is half of the start, so he started with 34.

solve.work: Backwards: after morning x with x/2-2=5, x=14; S/2-3=14, S=34. Check 34->14->5.

questions.stem: Tess buys 4 pencils and 3 erasers for 2.60 euros. Uma buys 4 pencils and 1 eraser of the same kinds for 1.80 euros. How many cents does one pencil cost?
questions.solution: The two purchases differ by 2 erasers and by 260 - 180 = 80 cents, so an eraser costs 40 cents. Then 4 pencils cost 180 - 40 = 140 cents and one pencil costs 35 cents.

questions.stem: Six boxes stand in a row, each holding a number. The numbers in any three neighbouring boxes add up to 30. The first box holds 8 and the fifth box holds 13. What number is in the sixth box?
questions.solution: The boxes 1-3 and 2-4 both add to 30, so box 4 equals box 1. In the same way box 5 equals box 2 and box 6 equals box 3. So the numbers repeat in threes: boxes 1, 2, 3 hold 8, 13 and 30 - 8 - 13 = 9. Box 6 holds 9.

questions.stem: The ages of Ana and Bea add up to 31, those of Bea and Cleo to 35, and those of Ana and Cleo to 38. How old is Cleo?
questions.solution: Adding all three sums counts everyone twice: 31 + 35 + 38 = 104, so the three ages add up to 52. Cleo is 52 - 31 = 21 years old.

questions.stem: Kim has 20 coins, all of them 5-cent or 10-cent coins, worth 1.60 euros in total. How many 10-cent coins does she have?
questions.solution: If all 20 coins were 5-cent coins they would be worth 100 cents. Each 10-cent coin adds 5 cents, and 160 - 100 = 60, so there are 60 / 5 = 12 ten-cent coins.

questions.stem: Three siblings share 1200 euros. The second gets 150 euros more than the first, and the third gets 150 euros more than the second. How many euros does the third get?
questions.solution: Compared with the first, the second gets 150 more and the third 300 more, 450 extra in all. Without it the three would share 750, so the first gets 250 and the third gets 250 + 300 = 550 euros.

questions.stem: Three jars contain 45 sweets altogether. Five sweets are moved from jar A to jar B, then 3 sweets are moved from jar B to jar C. Now all three jars hold the same number of sweets. How many sweets did jar A hold at the start?
questions.solution: In the end each jar holds 45 / 3 = 15 sweets. The only change to jar A was giving away 5, so it started with 15 + 5 = 20.

solve.work: Each ends with 15; A-5=15 so A=20 (B=13, C=12, total 45).

questions.stem: Seven years ago Hugo was three times as old as Iris. In seven years' time Hugo will be twice as old as Iris will be then. How old is Hugo now?
questions.solution: Let Iris be I years old now. Hugo was 3(I - 7) seven years ago, so he is 3(I - 7) + 7 = 3I - 14 now. In seven years: 3I - 7 = 2(I + 7), so I = 21 and Hugo is 3 x 21 - 14 = 49.

questions.stem: Two identical bottles: Mia's is $\frac{2}{5}$ full of juice and Nick's is $\frac{7}{10}$ full. Nick pours 90 millilitres into Mia's bottle, and then both bottles hold the same amount. How many millilitres does one full bottle hold?
questions.solution: Before pouring, Nick has $\frac{7}{10} - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{3}{10}$ of a bottle more than Mia. Pouring 90 ml changes the difference by 2 x 90 = 180 ml, so $\frac{3}{10}$ of a bottle is 180 ml and a full bottle is 600 ml.

solve.work: Difference 3/10; half of it, 3/20 of a bottle, is 90 ml, so bottle 600 ml.

questions.stem: A teacher wants to give every student in a class the same number of stickers. If she gives each student 4 stickers, 6 stickers are left over. If she wants to give each student 5 stickers, she is 9 stickers short. How many stickers does she have?
questions.solution: Going from 4 to 5 stickers each needs 6 + 9 = 15 more stickers, 1 more per student, so there are 15 students. She has 4 x 15 + 6 = 66 stickers.

questions.stem: Sara spends half of her money on a coat. Then she spends one third of what is left on a hat, and then one quarter of what is still left on lunch. She now has 18 euros. How many euros did she have at the start?
questions.solution: After lunch $\frac{3}{4}$ of the money was left, so before lunch she had 18 / $\frac{3}{4}$ = 24 euros. After the hat $\frac{2}{3}$ was left, so before the hat she had 36 euros. That was half of her money, so she started with 72 euros.

questions.skill: number wall with a sum rule
questions.stem: A number wall has four bricks in its bottom row, three bricks in the row above, then two, then one at the top. Every brick above the bottom row holds the sum of the two bricks directly below it. The bottom row reads, from left to right, 2, ?, ?, 6, and the top brick holds 62. What number is in the middle brick of the second row from the bottom?
questions.solution: Call the bottom row 2, b, c, 6. The top brick adds up to 2 + 3b + 3c + 6 = 62, so 3(b + c) = 54 and b + c = 18. The middle brick of the second row is b + c = 18.

solve.work: Bottom 2,a,b,6: top = 8+3(a+b)=62, so a+b=18, which is the middle brick of row 2.

questions.stem: Four parcels are weighed three at a time, giving the four readings 21 kg, 23 kg, 25 kg and 27 kg. How many kilograms does the heaviest parcel weigh?
questions.solution: Each parcel is on the scale in three of the four weighings, so 21 + 23 + 25 + 27 = 96 is three times the total weight, and the total is 32 kg. The smallest reading, 21 kg, is the weighing without the heaviest parcel, so the heaviest weighs 32 - 21 = 11 kg.

questions.stem: Ann, Ben and Cy have 120 euros altogether. First Ann gives Ben as much money as Ben already has. Then Ben gives Cy as much as Cy then has. Finally Cy gives Ann as much as Ann then has. After that each of them has 40 euros. How many euros did Ann have at the start?
questions.solution: Go backwards from (Ann, Ben, Cy) = (40, 40, 40). Before Cy's gift, Ann had 20 and Cy had 60: (20, 40, 60). Before Ben's gift, Cy had 30 and Ben 70: (20, 70, 30). Before Ann's gift, Ben had 35 and Ann 55: (55, 35, 30). Ann started with 55 euros.

questions.stem: Three pens of type A and two pens of type B cost 7.50 euros. Two pens of type A and three pens of type B cost 7.00 euros. How many cents does one pen of type B cost?
questions.solution: Multiply the second purchase by 3 and the first by 2: 6 A + 9 B cost 2100 cents and 6 A + 4 B cost 1500 cents. The difference is 5 B = 600 cents, so one pen of type B costs 120 cents. (Then A costs 170 cents.)

solve.work: Sum: a+b=290; difference: a-b=50; b=120 cents.

questions.stem: A teacher has a box of sweets. If she gives 5 sweets to each child, 17 sweets are left over. If she tries to give 6 sweets to each child, every child but the last gets 6 and the last child gets only 2. How many children are there?
questions.solution: With n children the box holds 5n + 17 sweets. Giving 6 to all but the last child and 2 to the last uses 6(n - 1) + 2 = 6n - 4 sweets. So 5n + 17 = 6n - 4, which gives n = 21.

questions.stem: A purse holds only 1-cent, 2-cent and 5-cent coins, 24 coins in all, worth 54 cents. There are twice as many 1-cent coins as 2-cent coins. How many 5-cent coins are there?
questions.solution: Let there be k two-cent coins, so 2k one-cent coins and 24 - 3k five-cent coins. The value is 2k + 2k + 5(24 - 3k) = 120 - 11k = 54, so k = 6. The number of 5-cent coins is 24 - 18 = 6.

solve.work: 2t ones, t twos, f fives: 3t+f=24, 4t+5f=54 gives t=6, f=6; check 12+12+30=54.

questions.stem: Mei cycles at a constant speed of 18 km/h. How many minutes does she need to ride 27 km?
questions.solution: 27 / 18 = 1.5 hours, which is 90 minutes.

questions.stem: The mean of five test scores is 14. Four of the scores are 10, 12, 15 and 17. What is the fifth score?
questions.solution: The five scores add up to 5 x 14 = 70. The four known scores add up to 54, so the fifth is 70 - 54 = 16.

questions.stem: A night train leaves at 22:40 and travels for 3 hours 35 minutes. At what time (on the 24-hour clock, the next day) does it arrive?
questions.solution: 22:40 plus 1 hour 20 minutes is midnight, 00:00. The remaining 3 h 35 min - 1 h 20 min = 2 h 15 min bring it to 02:15.

questions.stem: Omar walks at a constant 5 km/h. How many kilometres does he walk in 36 minutes?
questions.solution: 36 minutes is 0.6 hours, and 5 x 0.6 = 3 kilometres.

questions.skill: a new value changes the mean
questions.stem: The arithmetic mean of three numbers is 12. A fourth number is added, and the arithmetic mean of the four numbers is 14. What is the fourth number?
questions.solution: The first three add up to 36 and all four add up to 56, so the fourth number is 56 - 36 = 20.

questions.stem: Two cyclists are 60 km apart and ride towards each other, starting at the same moment, at constant speeds of 12 km/h and 18 km/h. After how many hours do they meet?
questions.solution: Together they close the gap at 12 + 18 = 30 km per hour, so they meet after 60 / 30 = 2 hours.

questions.stem: A clock loses 4 minutes every hour. It is set correctly at 12:00 noon. What time does it show when the real time is 3:00 p.m.?
questions.solution: In 3 hours it loses 3 x 4 = 12 minutes, so it shows 3:00 p.m. minus 12 minutes, which is 2:48 p.m.

questions.stem: A runner takes 90 seconds for each lap of a circular track and keeps the same pace all the time. How many complete laps does she finish in 20 minutes?
questions.solution: 20 minutes is 1200 seconds. 13 laps take 1170 seconds and 14 laps would take 1260 seconds, which is too long. She completes 13 laps.

questions.stem: A bus drives for 2 hours at a constant 60 km/h and then for 1 hour at a constant 30 km/h. What is its average speed over the three hours, in km/h?
questions.solution: The bus covers 120 + 30 = 150 km in 3 hours, so its average speed is 150 / 3 = 50 km/h.

questions.stem: The arithmetic mean of the ages of 5 players is 20 years. A player aged 30 leaves. What is the arithmetic mean of the ages of the other four, in years?
questions.solution: The ages add up to 100. Without the 30-year-old they add up to 70, and 70 / 4 = 17.5.

questions.stem: Sam walks along a straight path at a constant 4 km/h. Thirty minutes after Sam has left, Teo sets off from the same place along the same path on a bike at a constant 12 km/h. How many minutes after Teo's start does he catch up with Sam?
questions.solution: Sam has a head start of 2 km. Teo gains 12 - 4 = 8 km every hour, so he needs 2 / 8 = 0.25 hours, which is 15 minutes.

solve.work: Head start 2 km, closing at 8 km/h: 1/4 h = 15 min.

questions.stem: A watch gains 5 minutes every hour. It was set correctly at 8:00 a.m. Later the watch shows 9:00 p.m. What is the real time then?
questions.solution: In every real hour the watch runs 65 minutes. The watch has run 13 hours = 780 minutes, which is 780 / 65 = 12 real hours. The real time is 8:00 a.m. + 12 hours = 8:00 p.m.

solve.work: Watch runs 65 min per real 60; 13 watch hours = 780 min -> 720 real min = 12 h, so 8:00 p.m. (7:55 is the per-watch-hour misreading).

questions.skill: mean rises with a new value
questions.stem: The arithmetic mean of 6 numbers is 15. A seventh number is added, and the arithmetic mean of all 7 numbers is 17. What is the seventh number?
questions.solution: The six numbers add up to 90 and all seven add up to 119, so the seventh number is 119 - 90 = 29.

questions.stem: Two runners start together at the same point of a circular track 400 metres long and run in the same direction, at constant speeds of 5 m/s and 3 m/s. After how many seconds are they next together at the same point?
questions.solution: The faster runner gains 5 - 3 = 2 metres every second. They are together again when she has gained one full lap, 400 m, which takes 200 seconds.

solve.work: Relative 2 m/s, one lap 400 m: 200 s.

questions.skill: average speed of a round trip
questions.stem: A cyclist rides 12 km uphill at a constant 12 km/h and then returns along the same 12 km downhill at a constant 24 km/h. What is her average speed over the whole trip, in km/h?
questions.solution: Uphill takes 1 hour and downhill takes 0.5 hours. She rides 24 km in 1.5 hours, so her average speed is 24 / 1.5 = 16 km/h (not the 18 you get by averaging the two speeds).

questions.stem: Lena walks to school at a constant 6 km/h. When she rides her bike at a constant 18 km/h, the trip takes 20 minutes less. How many kilometres is the way to school?
questions.solution: Each kilometre takes 1/6 hour on foot and 1/18 hour by bike, a saving of 1/9 hour per kilometre. The total saving is 20 minutes = 1/3 hour, so the distance is (1/3) / (1/9) = 3 km.

questions.stem: Ana leaves town A at 9:00 a.m. and cycles towards town B at a constant 15 km/h. Ben leaves town B at 10:00 a.m. and cycles towards A along the same road at a constant 20 km/h. The towns are 85 km apart. At what time do they meet?
questions.solution: By 10:00 Ana has ridden 15 km, so 70 km separate them. They close the gap at 15 + 20 = 35 km/h, which takes 2 hours. They meet at 12:00 noon.

solve.work: By 10:00 Ana has 15 km; 70 km left at 35 km/h = 2 h: 12:00.

questions.stem: In a class there are 10 boys and 20 girls. The boys' mean score on a test is 60 and the girls' mean score is 75. What is the mean score of the whole class?
questions.solution: The boys score 600 points in all and the girls 1500, so the 30 students score 2100 points. The mean is 2100 / 30 = 70. (It is not 67.5, because there are more girls.)

questions.stem: A train 150 m long travels at a constant 15 m/s through a tunnel 450 m long. How many seconds pass from the moment the front of the train enters the tunnel until the back of the train leaves it?
questions.solution: The front must travel the tunnel's length plus the train's length, 450 + 150 = 600 m. At 15 m/s that takes 40 seconds.

questions.stem: The arithmetic mean of 8 numbers is 20. Two of them have an arithmetic mean of 26. What is the arithmetic mean of the other six numbers?
questions.solution: All eight add up to 160 and the two add up to 52, so the other six add up to 108 and their mean is 108 / 6 = 18.

questions.stem: A car travels 60 km at a constant 20 km/h, then another 60 km at a constant 30 km/h, and finally another 60 km at a constant 60 km/h. What is its average speed over the whole 180 km, in km/h?
questions.solution: The three parts take 3, 2 and 1 hours, 6 hours in all. The average speed is 180 / 6 = 30 km/h, lower than the average of the three speeds.

questions.stem: Two ants start at the same point of a circular track 120 cm long and walk around it in opposite directions at constant speeds of 4 cm/s and 8 cm/s. After how many seconds do they meet for the second time? (The start does not count as a meeting.)
questions.solution: Walking in opposite directions they close the gap by 4 + 8 = 12 cm every second. Each meeting needs one more full lap of 120 cm between them, so the first is after 10 seconds and the second after 20 seconds.

solve.work: Closing 12 cm/s, a meeting every 120/12=10 s; second at 20 s.

questions.stem: Towns P and Q are 120 km apart on a straight road. At the same moment a car leaves P for Q at a constant 60 km/h and a truck leaves Q for P at a constant 40 km/h. Each vehicle turns round as soon as it reaches the end of the road and drives back at the same speed without stopping. How many kilometres from P do the vehicles meet for the second time?
questions.solution: They meet first after 120 / 100 = 1.2 hours, 72 km from P. By the second meeting they have together covered 3 x 120 = 360 km, which takes 3.6 hours. In that time the car has driven 216 km: 120 km to Q and 96 km back, so it is 24 km from P.

solve.work: Second meeting after combined 360 km: t=3.6 h; car 216 km = to Q and 96 back, at 24 km from P; truck 144 km agrees; no meeting in between.

questions.stem: A wall clock with a 12-hour dial gains 6 minutes every hour. It is set exactly right at noon on Monday. After how many hours of real time will it next show exactly the right time again?
questions.solution: The clock shows the right time again when it has gained a full 12 hours, which is 720 minutes. At 6 minutes per hour that takes 720 / 6 = 120 hours.

solve.work: Must gain 12 h = 720 min at 6 min/h: 120 h.

questions.stem: The arithmetic mean of a student's first five scores is 82. After the sixth score, the mean of the six is 85, and after the seventh score, the mean of all seven is 84. What is the seventh score?
questions.solution: The first five add up to 410. Six scores add up to 6 x 85 = 510 and seven add up to 7 x 84 = 588. The seventh score is 588 - 510 = 78.

questions.stem: A school group walks from the hostel to a viewpoint at a constant 4 km/h, stays there for exactly 1 hour, and rides back along the same path by bike at a constant 12 km/h. From leaving the hostel until returning, they take 5 hours 20 minutes. How many kilometres is the viewpoint from the hostel?
questions.solution: Moving takes 5 h 20 min - 1 h = 4 h 20 min = 13/3 hours. Each kilometre takes 1/4 + 1/12 = 1/3 hour there and back, so the distance is (13/3) / (1/3) = 13 km. (Forgetting the stop gives 16.)

questions.stem: Two trains, 200 m and 300 m long, travel towards each other on parallel tracks at constant speeds of 20 m/s and 30 m/s. How many seconds pass from the moment their fronts meet until their ends have passed each other?
questions.solution: The trains approach each other at 20 + 30 = 50 m/s. They must pass by a combined length of 200 + 300 = 500 m, which takes 500 / 50 = 10 seconds.

questions.skill: mean and the number of items
questions.stem: The mean age of a group of children is 12 years. When their teacher, who is 36 years old, joins the group, the mean age of everyone becomes 13 years. How many children are in the group?
questions.solution: Each of the n children is 1 year below the new mean, and the teacher is 36 - 13 = 23 years above it. The differences balance, so n = 23 children. (Check: 12 x 23 + 36 = 312 = 13 x 24.)

questions.skill: a rematch with a head start
questions.stem: Katya and Lola run a 100 m race at constant speeds. When Katya crosses the finish line, Lola is exactly 10 m behind her. They race again over 100 m, but this time Katya starts 10 m behind the starting line while Lola starts on it. Both run at the same speeds as before. When Katya crosses the finish line, how many metres is Lola from it?
questions.solution: Lola's speed is 90 % of Katya's. Katya runs 110 m, and in that time Lola runs 90 % of 110 = 99 m. She is 1 m from the finish.

solve.work: Speeds 10:9; Katya runs 110 m while Lola runs 99 m, so Lola is 1 m short.

questions.stem: Two runners start together from the same point of a circular track 300 m long and run in the same direction, one at a constant 6 m/s and the other at a constant 4 m/s. During the first 11 minutes, how many times does the faster runner overtake the slower one? (The start does not count.)
questions.solution: The faster runner gains 2 m every second, so she overtakes the slower runner each time she gains 300 m, that is every 150 seconds: at 150, 300, 450 and 600 seconds. The next would be at 750 seconds, but 11 minutes is only 660 seconds. So she overtakes 4 times.

solve.work: 660 s * 2 m/s = 1320 m gained = 4.4 laps: 4 overtakes.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers are there from 37 to 92, counting both 37 and 92?
questions.solution: From 37 to 92 the difference is 55, and counting both ends adds one more. So there are 56 numbers.

questions.stem: At a chess club 7 players each shake hands exactly once with every other player before the games begin. How many handshakes are there in total?
questions.solution: Each of the 7 players shakes 6 hands, which counts every handshake twice. So there are 7 x 6 / 2 = 21 handshakes.

questions.stem: Ana, Bo and Cy stand in a line for a photo. Ana refuses to stand at the front. In how many different orders can the three of them stand?
questions.solution: There are 6 orders in all. Two of them have Ana at the front (Ana, Bo, Cy and Ana, Cy, Bo). So 6 - 2 = 4 orders remain.

solve.work: 3!=6 orders minus 2 with Ana at front = 4.

questions.skill: routes on a grid, right or down
questions.stem: A floor is tiled with square tiles in a grid of 2 rows and 3 columns. An ant walks along the tile edges from the top-left corner of the floor to the bottom-right corner, moving only right or down along edges. How many different routes can it take?
questions.solution: Every route has 3 moves right and 2 moves down, 5 moves in all. Choose which 2 of the 5 moves go down: 5 x 4 / 2 = 10 routes.

solve.work: Grid of 3x4 lattice points: 3 rights and 2 downs, C(5,2)=10.

questions.stem: How many multiples of 7 are strictly between 100 and 200?
questions.solution: The smallest multiple of 7 above 100 is 105 = 7 x 15 and the largest below 200 is 196 = 7 x 28. The multiplying numbers 15 to 28 give 28 - 15 + 1 = 14 multiples.

questions.stem: How many two-digit whole numbers have both digits odd?
questions.solution: The tens digit can be 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9 and so can the units digit. That gives 5 x 5 = 25 numbers.

solve.work: 5 odd tens digits x 5 odd units digits = 25.

questions.stem: A cafe lets you build a lunch from one of 3 soups, one of 4 sandwiches and one of 2 drinks. How many different lunches are possible?
questions.solution: Each choice is made independently, so multiply: 3 x 4 x 2 = 24 lunches.

questions.stem: A dark drawer holds 6 red, 6 blue and 6 green socks mixed together. Pedro takes socks out one at a time without looking. What is the smallest number of socks he must take to be sure of having two of the same colour?
questions.solution: In the worst case his first three socks are all different colours. The fourth sock must repeat a colour, so 4 socks are enough and 3 are not.

solve.work: 3 colours; 3 socks may all differ, the 4th forces a pair.

questions.stem: Eight players enter a knockout tennis tournament. In every match exactly one player is knocked out, and play continues until only one player is left. How many matches are played in total?
questions.solution: To leave one winner, 7 players must be knocked out. Each match knocks out exactly one, so 7 matches are played.

solve.work: Each match eliminates one; 7 must go.

questions.stem: How many of the whole numbers from 1 to 60 contain the digit 5 at least once? (The number 55 counts once.)
questions.solution: Numbers ending in 5: 5, 15, 25, 35, 45, 55 make 6. Numbers with tens digit 5: 50 to 59 make 10. The number 55 is in both lists, so 6 + 10 - 1 = 15.

questions.stem: A staircase has 8 steps. Lin climbs it taking either one or two steps at a time and ends exactly on the top step. In how many different ways can she climb it?
questions.solution: Let w(n) be the ways to reach step n. Then w(1) = 1, w(2) = 2 and each later value is the sum of the two before it: 3, 5, 8, 13, 21, 34. So w(8) = 34.

questions.stem: How many three-digit whole numbers have all three digits odd and all three digits different from each other?
questions.solution: The hundreds digit has 5 choices (1, 3, 5, 7, 9), the tens digit has 4 left, and the units digit has 3 left. So 5 x 4 x 3 = 60.

questions.stem: In a league every team plays every other team exactly once, and 45 matches are played in total. How many teams are in the league?
questions.solution: With n teams there are n(n - 1)/2 matches. For 45 matches, n(n - 1) = 90 = 10 x 9, so n = 10.

questions.stem: Ina, Joe, Kim, Leo and Mo stand in a row. Ina and Joe must stand next to each other, in either order. In how many different orders can the five of them stand?
questions.solution: Treat Ina and Joe as one block. The 4 units (block, Kim, Leo, Mo) can be ordered in 4! = 24 ways, and the block can be Ina-Joe or Joe-Ina. So 24 x 2 = 48.

questions.stem: How many of the whole numbers from 1 to 100 are multiples of 3 or multiples of 5 (or both)?
questions.solution: There are 33 multiples of 3 and 20 multiples of 5. The 6 multiples of 15 were counted twice, so 33 + 20 - 6 = 47.

questions.stem: How many three-digit whole numbers have digits that add up to 4?
questions.solution: Hundreds digit 1: the other two add to 3 (4 ways: 03, 12, 21, 30). Hundreds digit 2: they add to 2 (3 ways). Hundreds digit 3: they add to 1 (2 ways). Hundreds digit 4: 1 way. In all 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 10.

questions.stem: Four chairs, numbered 1 to 4, stand round a table, so chairs 1 and 4 are neighbours, as are 1 and 2, 2 and 3, and 3 and 4. Alex, Bea, Chen and Dara sit down, one to a chair. Alex and Bea refuse to sit on neighbouring chairs. In how many ways can the four be seated?
questions.solution: Alex and Bea must be on opposite chairs: either chairs 1 and 3, or chairs 2 and 4, which is 2 choices of pair. They can swap places (2 ways), and Chen and Dara can fill the other two chairs in 2 ways. So 2 x 2 x 2 = 8.

solve.work: Non-neighbouring chairs are opposite: Alex 4 choices, Bea 1, others 2: 8.

questions.stem: Twenty cards are numbered 1 to 20 and placed face down. What is the smallest number of cards you must pick to be sure that two of the picked cards add up to 21?
questions.solution: The numbers split into 10 pairs adding to 21: 1 and 20, 2 and 19, up to 10 and 11. Picking one card from each pair gives 10 cards with no pair adding to 21. An 11th card must complete a pair.

solve.work: 10 pairs summing to 21; 10 cards can avoid (one from each), 11 forces a pair.

questions.stem: A club trains on exactly 3 days of the week Monday to Sunday, and never on two days in a row. (Sunday and the Monday that follows are not counted as in a row.) In how many ways can the 3 training days be chosen?
questions.solution: List the days by number 1 to 7 and choose 3 with gaps between them. Starting from 1: 135, 136, 137, 146, 147, 157. Starting from 2: 246, 247, 257. Starting from 3: 357. That is 6 + 3 + 1 = 10.

solve.work: Non-adjacent 3 of 7 in a line: C(5,3)=10.

questions.stem: How many different triangles have whole-number side lengths and a perimeter of 12? Triangles that are congruent count as the same.
questions.solution: Write the sides as a, b, c with a at most b at most c. The two shorter sides must add to more than c, so c is less than 6. The triangles are 4, 4, 4, then 3, 4, 5, then 2, 5, 5. There are 3.

questions.stem: How many four-digit whole numbers have their four digits strictly increasing from left to right, such as 1358?
questions.solution: The digits are four different digits from 1 to 9 (0 cannot be used, because it would have to come first). Any chosen four digits can be written in only one increasing order. So the count is 9 x 8 x 7 x 6 / 24 = 126.

solve.work: Zero cannot appear; choose 4 of 1-9: C(9,4)=126.

questions.stem: In a group, every two members exchanged exactly one message, and 55 messages were sent in all. Then 3 new people join, and every new person exchanges one message with every other person in the enlarged group, including the other new people. (Pairs who have already exchanged a message do not do so again.) How many messages have been exchanged in total?
questions.solution: 55 = 11 x 10 / 2, so the group had 11 people. Now there are 14 people and every pair has exchanged exactly one message: 14 x 13 / 2 = 91.

solve.work: 55=C(11,2) so 11 people; 14 people give C(14,2)=91 in all.

questions.stem: Mia puts 12 identical coins into 3 identical boxes so that no box is empty. Because the boxes cannot be told apart, only the three numbers of coins matter, not which box holds which. How many different distributions are possible?

solve.work: Partitions of 12 into 3 positive parts: a=1:5, a=2:4, a=3:2, a=4:1 = 12.

questions.stem: A walker goes from the point (0, 0) to the point (3, 3) on a grid, moving one unit right or one unit up at each step. The piece of road joining (1, 1) and (2, 1) is closed. How many different routes are there?
questions.solution: Without the closure there are 20 routes. A route using the closed piece reaches (1, 1) in 2 ways, crosses the piece, then goes from (2, 1) to (3, 3) in 3 ways: 2 x 3 = 6 routes. So 20 - 6 = 14.

solve.work: 20 routes total; through the closed edge 2*3=6; 20-6=14.

questions.stem: A bag holds 10 red, 8 blue, 6 green and 4 yellow marbles. Marbles are drawn without looking. What is the smallest number that must be drawn to be certain of having at least 5 marbles of the same colour?
questions.solution: In the worst case there are 4 of each colour, which is possible because yellow has only 4 marbles. That is 16 marbles with no colour reaching 5. The 17th marble must make 5 of red, blue or green.

solve.work: 4 of each colour (16) avoids five alike; 17 forces it (all colours have >=4).

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 999 have digits that add up to 5?
questions.solution: Treat each number as three digits with leading zeros allowed. The number of digit triples with sum 5 is 6 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 1 = 21 (first digit 0 to 5 leaves 6 to 1 ways for the other two). The triple 000 does not have sum 5, so all 21 are valid numbers.

solve.work: Digit strings a+b+c=5 with leading zeros: C(7,2)=21.

questions.stem: Ava, Ben, Cho, Dan and Eve stand in a row. Ava must stand somewhere to the left of Ben (not necessarily next to him), and Cho must not stand at either end of the row. In how many different orders can they stand?
questions.solution: Cho takes one of the 3 middle places. The other four people fill the remaining 4 places in 24 ways, and in exactly half of them Ava is to the left of Ben. So 3 x 24 / 2 = 36.

solve.work: Cho in 3 middle places, others 4!=24 of which half have Ava left of Ben: 3*12=36.

questions.stem: In a tournament each pair of 7 teams plays exactly once. A win earns the winner 3 points and the loser 0; a draw earns each team 1 point. After all matches the teams have 55 points in total. How many matches ended in a draw?
questions.solution: There are 7 x 6 / 2 = 21 matches. A decided match gives 3 points and a draw gives 2 points in total. If every match were decided there would be 63 points, and each draw lowers this by 1. So 63 - 55 = 8 draws.

questions.stem: A grid is made of 3 rows and 4 columns of unit squares. How many rectangles of all sizes (squares included) have their sides along the grid lines?
questions.solution: A rectangle is fixed by choosing 2 of the 5 vertical lines and 2 of the 4 horizontal lines. That gives 10 x 6 = 60 rectangles.

questions.skill: digits all different and a divisor
questions.stem: How many three-digit whole numbers are multiples of 5 and have three different digits?
questions.solution: A multiple of 5 ends in 0 or 5. Ending in 0: the hundreds digit has 9 choices and the tens digit 8, giving 72. Ending in 5: the hundreds digit has 8 choices (not 0 or 5) and the tens digit 8 (not 5 or the hundreds digit), giving 64. Total 72 + 64 = 136.

questions.stem: Ana is taller than Ben. Ben is taller than Cy. Dan is shorter than Cy. Who is the second tallest of the four?
questions.solution: The order from tallest to shortest is Ana, Ben, Cy, Dan. The second tallest is Ben.

questions.stem: On an island every person is either a truth-teller, who always tells the truth, or a liar, who always lies. Rue is a liar. Rue says: Sol is a truth-teller. How many of the two people, Rue and Sol, are liars?
questions.solution: Rue's statement is a lie, so Sol is not a truth-teller, and Sol is a liar. Both Rue and Sol are liars, so the answer is 2.

solve.work: Rue lies, so Sol is a liar too: 2.

questions.stem: The digits 2, 4, 6, 8, 0 are written over and over in this order: 2 4 6 8 0 2 4 6 8 0 and so on. Which digit is in the 37th place?
questions.solution: The pattern repeats every 5 places. Place 35 ends the 7th block, so place 36 holds 2 and place 37 holds 4.

questions.stem: It is 10:00 in the morning on a Monday. What day and time will it be 50 hours later?
questions.solution: 48 hours is exactly 2 days, which brings us to Wednesday 10:00. Two more hours give Wednesday 12:00.

questions.stem: Seven odd whole numbers are added together. Which statement about their sum is correct?
choices: It is odd, whatever the seven numbers are
It is even, whatever the seven numbers are
It may be odd or even, depending on them
questions.answer: It is odd, whatever the seven numbers are
questions.solution: Odd numbers pair up to give even sums. Seven odd numbers make three pairs and one left over, so the total is even plus odd, which is odd.

solve.answer: It is odd, whatever the seven numbers are
solve.work: Odd count of odd numbers is odd.

questions.stem: A flea starts at 0 on a number line. It jumps 3 units to the right, then 2 units to the left, then 3 right, then 2 left, and so on. Where is it after 20 jumps?
questions.solution: Each pair of jumps (right 3, left 2) moves it 1 unit to the right. 20 jumps make 10 pairs, so it is at 10.

solve.work: Each pair of jumps nets +1; 10 pairs.

questions.stem: A two-digit number has a tens digit that is twice its units digit, and its two digits add up to 9. Which number is it?
questions.solution: If the units digit is u, the tens digit is 2u and u + 2u = 9, so u = 3. The number is 63.

questions.stem: Which even number between 40 and 60 leaves remainder 3 when divided by 7?
questions.solution: The numbers between 40 and 60 with remainder 3 are 45, 52 and 59. Only 52 is even.

solve.work: Numbers =3 mod 7 in range: 45,52,59; the even one is 52.

questions.stem: Five children stand in a queue. Eli is ahead of Fay. Gus is behind Fay but ahead of Hal. Ida is behind Hal. Counting from the front of the queue, at which place does Gus stand?
questions.solution: The clues give the chain Eli, Fay, Gus, Hal, Ida from front to back. Gus is third.

solve.work: Order Eli, Fay, Gus, Hal, Ida; Gus third.

questions.stem: Truth-tellers always tell the truth and liars always lie. Zoe is a truth-teller and says: Yan is a liar. Yan says: Xia is a liar. How many of Zoe, Yan and Xia are truth-tellers?
questions.solution: Zoe tells the truth, so Yan is a liar. Yan's statement is false, so Xia is not a liar and tells the truth. Zoe and Xia are truth-tellers: 2.

solve.work: Yan is a liar, so Xia is a truth-teller: Zoe and Xia.

questions.stem: Three people are each either a knight, who always tells the truth, or a liar, who always lies. A says: Exactly one of the three of us is a liar. B says: Exactly two of the three of us are liars. C says: All three of us are liars. How many of them are liars?
questions.solution: If C told the truth, C would be a liar, which is impossible, so C is a liar. A and B cannot both be right, so at most one is a knight. If A were a knight, B would also be a knight, a contradiction. So A is a liar, and B is a knight: exactly A and C are liars, which fits. The answer is 2.

solve.work: Statements exclusive; all liars makes C true, so exactly one truthful, B: 2 liars.

questions.stem: The digits 1, 3, 9, 7 are written over and over in this order: 1 3 9 7 1 3 9 7 and so on. What is the sum of the first 50 digits?
questions.solution: One block of four digits adds to 20. 50 digits are 12 full blocks plus 2 more digits: 12 x 20 + 1 + 3 = 244.

questions.stem: Five friends sit in seats numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Gil sits in one of the two end seats. Hana sits next to Gil. Ivo sits somewhere to the left of Hana. Jon sits next to Ivo. Kim sits somewhere to the right of Jon. Who sits in seat 3?
questions.solution: Hana has Ivo on her left, so Gil must be at the right end in seat 5 with Hana in seat 4. Ivo and Jon are neighbours somewhere in seats 1 to 3, and Kim is to the right of Jon, so Kim fills the remaining seat. Ivo and Jon take seats 1 and 2, so Kim is in seat 3.

solve.work: Gil seat 5, Hana 4 (Gil in 1 fails); Ivo/Jon in 1-2, Kim 3 in every case.

questions.stem: A grasshopper starts at 0 on a number line and makes exactly 4 jumps. Each jump is either 3 units to the right or 5 units to the right. Which of these positions can it end on?
questions.solution: If it makes k jumps of 3 and 4 - k jumps of 5, it lands on 20 - 2k, which is always even. Of the options only 16 is even, and it is reached with k = 2.

questions.stem: Four closed boxes are labelled A, B, C and D, and a coin is in exactly one of them. The label on A says: The coin is in this box. The label on B says: The coin is not in this box. The label on C says: The coin is in box B. The label on D says: The coin is not in this box. Exactly one of the four labels is true. In which box is the coin?
questions.solution: Test each box. Coin in A: A and B and D are true, too many. Coin in B: C and D are true. Coin in C: B and D are true. Coin in D: only the label on B is true, since A, C and D are false. So the coin is in D.

solve.work: Coin in D: only B's label true; A, B, C each give two true labels.

questions.stem: What is the smallest whole number greater than 50 that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 3 and remainder 2 when divided by 4?
questions.solution: Numbers with remainder 2 on division by 4 are 54, 58, 62 and so on. Of these, 54 leaves remainder 0 on division by 3, and 58 leaves remainder 1. So the answer is 58.

solve.work: n=10 mod 12: 58 is the first above 50.

questions.skill: position in a long letter sequence
questions.stem: The word TRIANGLE is written over and over without gaps: TRIANGLETRIANGLE and so on. Which letter stands in the 2027th place?
questions.solution: The word has 8 letters and 2027 = 8 x 253 + 3. So place 2027 holds the same letter as place 3 of the word, which is I.

questions.stem: A lock code is a three-digit number with three different digits. The digits multiply to 40 and add up to 14. The code is odd, is greater than 500, and its tens digit is larger than its hundreds digit. What is the code?
questions.solution: The only three different digits with product 40 and sum 14 are 1, 5 and 8. Odd numbers over 500 from them are 581, 815 and 851. Only 581 has a tens digit larger than the hundreds digit.

solve.work: Digits {1,5,8} (only triple with product 40, sum 14); odd, >500, tens>hundreds gives 581.

questions.stem: A vase was broken by exactly one of four children: Ola, Pim, Quin or Rex. Ola says: Pim did it. Pim says: Quin did it. Quin says: I did not do it. Rex says nothing. Exactly two of the three statements are true. Who broke the vase?
questions.solution: Test each child as the culprit. If Ola or Rex did it, only Quin's statement is true. If Quin did it, only Pim's statement is true. If Pim did it, Ola's and Quin's statements are true, exactly two.

solve.work: Pim: true, false, true = 2 true; other culprits give 1.

questions.stem: A bug starts at 0 on a number line. It jumps 5 units to the right, then 8 units to the left, then 5 right, then 8 left, and so on. After how many jumps is it at -9 for the first time?
questions.solution: Positions after the jumps are 5, -3, 2, -6, -1, -9. After 2 jumps it is at -3, after 4 jumps at -6 and after 6 jumps at -9. After an odd number of jumps it is at 5 minus a multiple of 3, never -9, so the first time is after 6 jumps.

solve.work: After 2k jumps at -3k; after 2k+1 at 5-3k; -9 first at 6 jumps.

questions.stem: Five people stand in a row. Each is either a truth-teller or a liar. The first says: Exactly 1 of us five is a liar. The second says: Exactly 2 of us are liars. The third says 3, the fourth says 4, and the fifth says 5 in the same way. How many liars are there?
questions.solution: Two different statements cannot both be true, so at most one person tells the truth. If nobody did, there would be 5 liars and the fifth would be telling the truth, a contradiction. So exactly one is truthful, there are 4 liars, and the fourth person's statement is the true one.

solve.work: Exclusive statements; zero true makes the 5th true, so one truthful: 4 liars.

questions.stem: A list begins 1, 1, 2, 0, 2, 2, ... Every term after the first two is the remainder when the sum of the two terms just before it is divided by 3. What is the sum of the first 2026 terms?
questions.solution: Continuing gives 1, 1, 2, 0, 2, 2, 1, 0, then the list repeats from 1, 1. One block of 8 terms adds to 9. 2026 = 8 x 253 + 2, so the sum is 253 x 9 + 1 + 1 = 2279.

questions.stem: A flea starts at 0 on a number line. Its n-th jump is n units long, to the right if n is odd and to the left if n is even. So it jumps 1 right, 2 left, 3 right, 4 left, and so on. Where is it after 2025 jumps?
questions.solution: Group the jumps in pairs: 1 right and 2 left moves it -1, then 3 right and 4 left moves it -1 again. After 1012 such pairs (2024 jumps) it is at -1012. The 2025th jump is 2025 to the right, giving 2025 - 1012 = 1013.

questions.skill: extreme case with knights and liars
questions.stem: Ten people sit at a round table. Each is a knight, who always tells the truth, or a liar, who always lies. Each person says: Both of my neighbours are liars. What is the smallest possible number of knights?
questions.solution: A knight has two liars as neighbours, so no two knights are adjacent. A liar's statement is false, so every liar has at least one knight neighbour. Each knight can serve at most 2 liars, so 2k is at least 10 - k, giving k at least 4. Four knights work, for example in the seat pattern K L L K L L K L K L round the table.

solve.work: Knights form an independent dominating set of C10; minimum ceil(10/3)=4, e.g. seats 1,4,7,9.

questions.stem: Seven coins lie in a row, all showing heads. In each move you must turn over exactly three coins of your choice. What is the smallest number of moves after which all seven coins show tails?
questions.solution: Each coin must be turned an odd number of times, so the total number of turns is at least 7 and is odd. Every move gives 3 turns, so the total is a multiple of 3: the first possibility is 9 turns, which needs 3 moves. Three moves do work: turn coins 1, 2, 3, then 1, 4, 5, then 1, 6, 7. So 3 moves.

solve.work: Need odd flips each, 3m>=7 and odd: m=3, e.g. {1,2,7},{3,4,7},{5,6,7}.

questions.stem: How many whole numbers from 1 to 1000 leave remainder 1 when divided by 2, remainder 2 when divided by 3, remainder 3 when divided by 4 and remainder 4 when divided by 5?
questions.solution: Each condition says the number is one short of a multiple, so the number plus 1 is a multiple of 2, 3, 4 and 5, that is of 60. The numbers are 59, 119, 179, and so on up to 959 (1019 is too big). 59 + 60k up to 959 gives k from 0 to 15, which is 16 numbers.

questions.skill: deduce a number from true-or-false statements
questions.stem: A secret whole number is between 1 and 60. Four friends each make two statements, and exactly one statement of each friend is true. Friend 1: it is a multiple of 6; it is a multiple of 8. Friend 2: it is greater than 40; it is a multiple of 5. Friend 3: it is a multiple of 7; it leaves remainder 2 when divided by 4. Friend 4: it is even; it is a multiple of 3. What is the number?
questions.solution: Every multiple of 6 or 8 is even, so Friend 4's true statement must be the even one, and the number is not a multiple of 3. So for Friend 1 it is a multiple of 8 but not of 6: 8, 16, 32, 40 or 56. Friend 2 needs exactly one of: greater than 40, multiple of 5, which leaves 40 and 56. Friend 3 needs exactly one of: multiple of 7, remainder 2 mod 4; 40 has neither and 56 has only the first. So the number is 56.

solve.work: Multiple of 6 makes friend 4 say two truths, so multiple of 8 not 3; then multiple of 7: 56; friend 2 checks.

questions.stem: Four houses stand in a row, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right, painted red, blue, green and yellow in some order. Ana, Ben, Cai and Dee each live in a different house. The red house is somewhere to the left of the blue house. The yellow house is somewhere to the right of the blue house. Ben lives in the red house. Cai lives next door to Ben. Cai lives somewhere to the right of Ana. What colour is Ana's house?
questions.solution: Red, blue and yellow appear in that order from left to right, and green fits somewhere. Ana must be left of Cai, and Cai is next to Ben in the red house. If red were first, Ana would have no house to the left of Cai (house 1 is Ben's, house 2 is Cai's). So green is first, red is second, and Ana lives in house 1, the green one, with Cai in the blue house.

solve.work: Only colour order G R B Y works (Ben at 2, Cai at 3, Ana at 1).

questions.stem: The whole numbers are written one after another without gaps: 123456789101112131415 and so on. Which digit stands in the 2026th place?
questions.solution: The 9 one-digit numbers fill 9 places and the 90 two-digit numbers fill 180 more, so 189 places are used up to 99. The remaining 2026 - 189 = 1837 places are filled by three-digit numbers: 1837 = 3 x 612 + 1. So the place is the first digit of the 613th three-digit number, 100 + 612 = 712, which is 7.

solve.work: 189 digits to 99; 1837 = 3*612+1, so first digit of 712: 7.

questions.stem: What is the last digit of the product of 2026 sevens, that is $7 \times 7 \times \ldots \times 7$ with 2026 factors?
questions.solution: The last digits of 7, 49, 343, 2401 are 7, 9, 3, 1 and then repeat with period 4. Since 2026 = 4 x 506 + 2, the last digit is the second one of the cycle, which is 9.

questions.stem: A rectangle is 14 cm long and 6 cm wide. A square has the same perimeter as the rectangle. What is the area of the square, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: The rectangle has perimeter $2(14+6)=40$ cm, so the square has side $40\div 4=10$ cm and area $10\times 10=100$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$ the sides $AB$ and $AC$ are equal and $\angle BAC = 48^\circ$. How many degrees is $\angle ABC$?
questions.solution: The base angles are equal, so $\angle ABC=(180-48)\div 2=66$ degrees.

questions.stem: Points $P$, $O$, $Q$ lie on a straight line with $O$ between $P$ and $Q$. Two more rays, $OA$ and $OB$, start at $O$ on the same side of line $PQ$, and going round from $OP$ to $OQ$ the rays come in the order $OP$, $OA$, $OB$, $OQ$. If $\angle POA = 35^\circ$ and $\angle BOQ = 50^\circ$, how many degrees is $\angle AOB$?
questions.solution: The three angles $POA$, $AOB$ and $BOQ$ together fill the straight angle $POQ=180^\circ$, so $\angle AOB=180-35-50=95$ degrees.

questions.stem: A rectangle is made of 6 equal squares placed in 2 rows of 3 squares, with no gaps or overlaps. Its perimeter is 40 cm. What is its area, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: If a small square has side $s$, the big rectangle is $3s$ by $2s$ with perimeter $10s=40$, so $s=4$ cm. The area is $6\times 4^2=96$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: A square sheet of paper has side 10 cm. It is folded exactly in half along a line joining the midpoints of two opposite sides, giving a rectangle. What is the perimeter of this rectangle, in cm?
questions.solution: The folded sheet measures 10 cm by 5 cm, so its perimeter is $2\times(10+5)=30$ cm.

questions.stem: $M$ is the midpoint of segment $AB$, and $AB = 18$ cm. $N$ is the midpoint of segment $AM$. How many centimetres long is segment $NB$?
An equilateral triangle has perimeter 36 cm. A square has the same side length as this triangle. What is the perimeter of the square, in cm?
questions.solution: The triangle's side is $36\div 3=12$ cm, so the square has perimeter $4\times 12=48$ cm.

questions.skill: half a rectangle cut by a diagonal
questions.stem: Square $ABCD$ has side 12 cm. $P$ is the midpoint of $AB$ and $Q$ is the midpoint of $CD$. The segment $PQ$ cuts the square into two rectangles. The rectangle $APQD$ is then cut along its diagonal $AQ$ into two triangles. What is the area of triangle $APQ$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Rectangle $APQD$ is 6 cm by 12 cm, area 72 cm$^2$. A diagonal splits it into two equal triangles, so triangle $APQ$ has area $72\div 2=36$ cm$^2$.

solve.work: APQD is 6 by 12, area 72; half is 36.

questions.stem: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $\angle A = 90^\circ$, $\angle B = 75^\circ$ and $\angle C = 110^\circ$. How many degrees is $\angle D$?
questions.solution: The angles of a quadrilateral add up to $360^\circ$, so $\angle D=360-90-75-110=85$ degrees.

questions.skill: circles in a row inside a rectangle
questions.stem: Three circles, each of radius 3 cm, are in a row so that each circle touches the next one. A rectangle has two sides parallel to the row and touches all three circles from outside, with its short sides touching the first and the last circle. What is the perimeter of this rectangle, in cm?
questions.solution: The row is $3\times 6=18$ cm long and each circle is 6 cm across, so the rectangle is 18 cm by 6 cm. Its perimeter is $2\times(18+6)=48$ cm.

questions.skill: triangles on opposite sides of a rectangle
questions.stem: In rectangle $ABCD$ we have $AB = 10$ cm and $BC = 6$ cm. The point $P$ lies inside the rectangle and the area of triangle $PAB$ is 14 cm$^2$. What is the area of triangle $PCD$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: The distances from $P$ to $AB$ and to $CD$ add up to $BC=6$ cm, and $AB=CD=10$ cm, so the two triangles have areas adding up to $\frac{1}{2}\times 10\times 6=30$ cm$^2$. Hence $PCD$ has area $30-14=16$ cm$^2$.

solve.work: Heights to AB and CD sum to 6, so the two areas sum to 30; 30-14 = 16.

questions.stem: The angles of a triangle are in the ratio $2:3:7$. How many degrees is the largest angle?
questions.solution: The ratio has $2+3+7=12$ parts, each worth $180\div 12=15$ degrees. The largest angle is $7\times 15=105$ degrees.

questions.skill: perimeter with a notch cut out
questions.stem: A rectangle measures 10 cm by 8 cm. A smaller rectangle measuring 4 cm by 3 cm is cut out of one of its corners, leaving an L-shaped piece. What is the perimeter of the L-shaped piece, in cm?
questions.solution: Cutting a rectangular notch from a corner removes a stretch of the outline and replaces it with a path of the same total length (4 cm and 3 cm), so the perimeter stays $2\times(10+8)=36$ cm.

solve.work: Cutting a corner rectangle leaves the perimeter unchanged: 2(10+8) = 36.

questions.stem: Five identical rectangles are fitted together without gaps or overlaps to make one large rectangle. Two of them lie side by side along the top, each with its longer side horizontal. Below them three stand side by side, each with its longer side vertical, and the two rows have the same total width. A small rectangle has perimeter 20 cm. What is the perimeter of the large rectangle, in cm?
questions.solution: Let a small rectangle be $l$ by $w$ with $l+w=10$. The rows are equally wide, so $2l=3w$, giving $l=6$, $w=4$. The large rectangle is $12$ wide and $w+l=10$ tall, so its perimeter is $2\times(12+10)=44$ cm.

solve.work: 2L = 3W, L+W = 10, so L = 6, W = 4; large is 12 by 10, perimeter 44.

questions.skill: touching circles and triangle of centres
questions.stem: Three circles have radii 2 cm, 3 cm and 4 cm, and each circle touches each of the other two from outside. The three centres are joined to form a triangle. What is the perimeter of this triangle, in cm?
questions.solution: The distance between the centres of two circles that touch from outside is the sum of their radii: $2+3=5$, $3+4=7$ and $2+4=6$. The perimeter is $5+7+6=18$ cm.

questions.skill: triangle inside a square with midpoints
questions.stem: Square $ABCD$ has side 8 cm. $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$ and $N$ is the midpoint of $CD$. What is the area of triangle $AMN$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Cut the three corner triangles off the square: $ABM$ has area $\frac12\times 8\times 4=16$, $ADN$ also 16, and $MCN$ has area $\frac12\times 4\times 4=8$. So $AMN$ has area $64-16-16-8=24$ cm$^2$.

questions.skill: angle chasing in an isosceles triangle
questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$ we have $AB = AC$ and $\angle BAC = 40^\circ$. The point $D$ lies on side $AC$ so that $BD = BC$. How many degrees is $\angle ABD$?
questions.solution: Since $AB=AC$, $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=70^\circ$. As $BD=BC$, triangle $BCD$ has $\angle BDC=\angle BCD=70^\circ$, so $\angle CBD=40^\circ$. Then $\angle ABD=70-40=30$ degrees.

solve.work: Base angles 70; in BCD angles 70, 70, 40 so DBC = 40; ABD = 70-40 = 30.

questions.stem: A paper strip is 30 cm long and 4 cm wide. It is folded in half so that its length becomes 15 cm, and then folded in half the same way again, so that its length is halved once more. All layers lie exactly on top of each other. What is the perimeter, in cm, of the folded shape?
questions.solution: After two folds the shape is a rectangle $30\div 4=7.5$ cm long and 4 cm wide, so its perimeter is $2\times(7.5+4)=23$ cm.

solve.work: Two halvings of the length: 30 -> 15 -> 7.5 cm, width stays 4 cm; perimeter = 2(7.5+4) = 23 cm.

questions.stem: A rectangular photo measures 30 cm by 20 cm. It is mounted in a frame of the same width, 3 cm, along all four sides, so the frame and photo together form a larger rectangle. What is the area of the frame alone, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: The outer rectangle is $30+6=36$ by $20+6=26$, with area $936$ cm$^2$. Taking away the photo's $600$ cm$^2$ leaves $336$ cm$^2$.

questions.skill: areas with midpoints in a triangle
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has area 48 cm$^2$. $D$ is the midpoint of side $BC$, and $E$ is the midpoint of segment $AD$. What is the area of triangle $BED$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Median $AD$ splits triangle $ABC$ into two triangles of area 24 cm$^2$. In triangle $ABD$, the point $E$ is the midpoint of $AD$, so $BED$ is half of $ABD$: $24\div 2=12$ cm$^2$.

solve.work: ABD = 24, BED is half of it = 12.

questions.skill: triangle from midpoints of three sides
questions.stem: Rectangle $ABCD$ has $AB = 16$ cm and $BC = 10$ cm. $E$, $F$ and $G$ are the midpoints of sides $AB$, $BC$ and $CD$ respectively. What is the area of triangle $EFG$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Take $E$ and $G$ as the base: they are 10 cm apart ($E$ is on $AB$, $G$ on $CD$, directly opposite, since both are midpoints), and $F$ is on $BC$ at distance $8$ cm from the line $EG$. The area is $\frac12\times 10\times 8=40$ cm$^2$.

solve.work: EG = 10 (vertical), F at distance 8 from it: area 40.

questions.skill: ratio of segments from similar triangles
questions.stem: Square $ABCD$ has side 12 cm, with vertices in order. $M$ is the midpoint of side $CD$. The segment $AM$ crosses the diagonal $BD$ at the point $P$. What is the area of triangle $ABP$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Segments $AB$ (12 cm) and $DM$ (6 cm) are parallel, so triangles $ABP$ and $MDP$ are similar with ratio $2:1$. Thus $BP:PD=2:1$ and $P$ is $\frac23$ of the way along $BD$. Triangle $ABP$ is $\frac23$ of triangle $ABD$, which has area 72 cm$^2$, giving 48 cm$^2$.

questions.stem: Square $ABCD$ has vertices in order. The point $E$ lies inside the square so that triangle $ABE$ is equilateral. How many degrees is $\angle CED$?
questions.solution: $\angle DAE=90-60=30^\circ$ and $AD=AE$, so $\angle AED=(180-30)\div 2=75^\circ$; likewise $\angle BEC=75^\circ$. The angles at $E$ add to $360^\circ$ and $\angle AEB=60^\circ$, so $\angle CED=360-60-75-75=150$ degrees.

solve.work: DAE = 30, ADE = 75, EDC = 15, likewise ECD = 15; CED = 150.

questions.stem: In triangle $ABC$ we have $AB = AC$. The point $D$ lies on side $BC$ so that $DA = DB$ and also $CD = CA$. How many degrees is $\angle BAC$?
questions.solution: Let $\angle B=x$. Then $\angle C=x$ and $\angle BAD=x$ (as $DA=DB$), so the exterior angle $\angle ADC=2x$. As $CD=CA$, $\angle CAD=\angle CDA=2x$. Then $\angle BAC=3x$ and also $180-2x$, so $x=36$ and $\angle BAC=108$ degrees.

solve.work: B = C = x, BAD = x, CAD = (180-x)/2, sum 180-2x gives x = 36; BAC = 108 (configuration checks out).

questions.stem: Two circles, of radius 4 cm and 9 cm, touch each other from outside. Both lie on the same side of a straight line and both touch that line. How many centimetres apart are the two points where the circles touch the line?
