questions.solution: The centres are 13 cm apart and the vertical difference of the centres is $9-4=5$ cm. By Pythagoras the horizontal distance, which equals the distance between the touching points, is $\sqrt{13^2-5^2}=12$ cm.

questions.skill: areas of triangles sharing a height
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has area 48 cm$^2$. The point $D$ lies on side $BC$ with $BD:DC=1:3$, and the point $E$ lies on side $AC$ with $AE:EC=2:1$. What is the area of triangle $BDE$, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Triangle $BCE$ has the same height from $B$ as $ABC$ and $EC=\frac13 AC$, so its area is 16 cm$^2$. Triangle $DCE$ is $\frac34$ of triangle $BCE$ (same height from $E$, base $DC=\frac34 BC$), so 12 cm$^2$. Then $BDE=16-12=4$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: A rectangle has whole-number side lengths in centimetres and area 36 cm$^2$. What is the difference, in cm, between the greatest and the smallest possible perimeter of such a rectangle?
questions.solution: The rectangles are $1\times 36$, $2\times 18$, $3\times 12$, $4\times 9$ and $6\times 6$, with perimeters 74, 40, 30, 26 and 24. The difference between the greatest and the smallest is $74-24=50$ cm.

questions.stem: Four identical rectangles are placed inside a large square, one at each corner, turning in the same direction like a pinwheel, so that they fill the large square exactly except for a small square hole in the middle. The large square has perimeter 60 cm and the hole has side 3 cm. What is the area of one rectangle, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Let the rectangle be $a$ by $b$ with $a>b$. The large square has side $a+b=15$ and the hole has side $a-b=3$, so $a=9$ and $b=6$. One rectangle has area $9\times 6=54$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: Square $ABCD$ has side 8 cm, with vertices in order, and $M$ is the midpoint of side $CD$. The paper is folded along a straight line so that corner $A$ lands exactly on $M$. The fold line meets side $AD$ at the point $P$. How many centimetres long is $AP$?
questions.solution: After folding, $P$ stays on the fold line, so $PA=PM$. Let $AP=x$, so $PD=8-x$ and $DM=4$. By Pythagoras in the right triangle $PDM$, $x^2=(8-x)^2+16$, i.e. $16x=80$ and $x=5$ cm.

questions.skill: height of a right triangle by two areas
questions.stem: Triangle $ABC$ has a right angle at $B$, with $AB = 9$ cm, $BC = 12$ cm and $AC = 15$ cm. How many centimetres is the distance from $B$ to the line $AC$?
questions.solution: The area is $\frac12\times 9\times 12=54$ cm$^2$. Using $AC=15$ as the base, the height from $B$ is $h$ with $\frac12\times 15\times h=54$, so $h=7.2$ cm.

questions.skill: cubes remaining after a layer is removed
questions.stem: A big cube is built from $5\times5\times5=125$ small cubes. The whole top layer of 25 small cubes is taken away. How many small cubes are left?
questions.solution: One layer of $5\times5=25$ cubes is removed, so $125-25=100$ small cubes remain.

questions.skill: die with opposite faces summing to 7
questions.stem: On a standard die, opposite faces add up to 7. A die sits on a table with the number 5 on its top face. What is the sum of the numbers on its four side faces?
questions.solution: All six faces add up to $1+2+3+4+5+6=21$. The top is 5 and the bottom is $7-5=2$, so the four sides add up to $21-5-2=14$.

questions.stem: A cuboid measures 4 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. What is its total surface area, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: The faces come in three equal pairs: $4\times3=12$, $4\times2=8$ and $3\times2=6$. The total is $2\times(12+8+6)=52$ cm$^2$.

questions.skill: edges and vertices of a pyramid
questions.stem: A pyramid has a square base and four triangular faces that meet at one apex. How many edges and vertices does it have in total, counting the edges and the vertices together?
questions.solution: There are 4 edges around the base and 4 edges up to the apex, so 8 edges. There are 4 base vertices and the apex, so 5 vertices. The total is $8+5=13$.

questions.skill: axes of symmetry of a regular polygon
questions.stem: How many axes of symmetry (mirror lines) does a regular hexagon have?
questions.solution: A regular polygon with $n$ sides has $n$ axes of symmetry. Here 3 axes join opposite vertices and 3 join midpoints of opposite sides, so there are 6.

solve.work: 3 through opposite vertices, 3 through opposite edge midpoints.

questions.skill: letters with a vertical axis of symmetry
questions.stem: The capital letters A, B, E, F, H, M, N, T, Z are written in plain block form. How many of them look the same when reflected in a vertical mirror line drawn through their middle?
questions.solution: A, H, M and T are symmetric about a vertical line. B and E are symmetric about a horizontal line only, and F, N and Z have no vertical mirror line. So the answer is 4.

solve.work: A, H, M, T have a vertical mirror line; B, E, F, N, Z do not.

questions.skill: unpainted cubes inside a painted cube
questions.stem: A cube with edge 4 is built from $4\times4\times4=64$ small cubes. Its whole outside surface is painted, and then it is taken apart into the small cubes. How many small cubes have no paint on them at all?
questions.solution: The cubes with no paint are those inside, forming a cube that is $4-2=2$ cubes along each edge. That is $2\times2\times2=8$ cubes.

questions.stem: A box is a cuboid with a base 6 cm long and 5 cm wide. Its volume is 120 cm$^3$. How many centimetres tall is it?
questions.solution: Volume equals base area times height, so the height is $120\div(6\times5)=4$ cm.

questions.skill: rotational symmetry of a regular polygon
questions.stem: What is the smallest angle, in degrees, by which a regular pentagon can be turned about its centre so that it lands exactly on itself?
questions.solution: The five vertices are spread evenly around the centre, so the smallest turn is $360\div5=72$ degrees.

questions.stem: A cube is made by folding a net of six squares, each with area 9 cm$^2$. What is the volume of the cube, in cm$^3$?
questions.solution: Each square has area 9 cm$^2$, so the edge of the cube is 3 cm and the volume is $3\times3\times3=27$ cm$^3$.

questions.skill: cubes with exactly one painted face
questions.stem: A cube with edge 5 is built from 125 small cubes. Its whole outside surface is painted and then it is taken apart into the small cubes. How many small cubes have paint on exactly one face?
questions.solution: Such cubes lie in the middle of a face, away from its edges: each face has a $3\times3=9$ block of them. With 6 faces, there are $6\times9=54$.

questions.skill: faces meeting at a vertex of a die
questions.stem: On a standard die, opposite faces add up to 7. At each of the 8 vertices three faces meet. At how many of the 8 vertices is the sum of the three numbers meeting there greater than 10?
questions.solution: At each vertex there is one face from each opposite pair: one of $\{1,6\}$, one of $\{2,5\}$, one of $\{3,4\}$. The 8 sums are 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, and exactly four of them (11, 12, 14, 15) exceed 10.

solve.work: Vertices are all 8 choices from {1,6},{2,5},{3,4}; sums 15,14,12,11 exceed 10, the others are 10,9,7,6.

questions.skill: surface area of two glued cubes
questions.stem: Two cubes, each with edge 3 cm, are glued together face to face so that the faces coincide exactly, forming a cuboid. What is the surface area of the cuboid, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: The cuboid measures $3\times3\times6$ cm. Its surface area is $2\times(9+18+18)=90$ cm$^2$. (Two separate cubes have $108$, and gluing hides two faces of 9 cm$^2$ each.)

questions.stem: A net is made of six squares numbered 1 to 6. Squares 1, 2, 3 and 4 form a row in this order from left to right, joined along whole sides. Square 5 is joined to the upper side of square 2, and square 6 is joined to the lower side of square 3. The net is folded into a cube. Which square ends up opposite square 3?
questions.solution: Squares 1, 2, 3, 4 wrap round the cube as a band of four side faces, so the squares at distance two in the row are opposite: 1 faces 3, and 2 faces 4. Squares 5 and 6 form the top and the bottom.

solve.work: In a row of four, 1-3 and 2-4 are opposite; 5 and 6 are opposite.

questions.skill: axes and angle of a regular polygon
questions.stem: A regular polygon is turned about its centre. The smallest angle by which it can be turned to land exactly on itself is $24^\circ$. How many axes of symmetry does this polygon have?
questions.solution: The polygon has $360\div24=15$ sides, and a regular polygon with 15 sides has 15 axes of symmetry.

questions.skill: water level after a solid is submerged
questions.stem: A tank is a cuboid with a square base of 20 cm by 20 cm and contains water 10 cm deep. A solid cube with edge 10 cm is lowered into the tank and rests on the bottom, completely under the water, and no water spills out. How many centimetres deep is the water now?
questions.solution: The water starts at $20\times20\times10=4000$ cm$^3$. The water and the cube together fill $4000+1000=5000$ cm$^3$ of the tank, whose base is 400 cm$^2$, so the depth is $5000\div400=12.5$ cm. This is above the cube's top (10 cm), so the cube is covered.

solve.work: Water 4000; first 10 cm holds 300*10 = 3000, the remaining 1000 over area 400 gives 2.5; depth 12.5 (cube submerged).

questions.stem: Among the capital letters, exactly H, I, N, O, S, X and Z look the same after a half-turn (rotation by $180^\circ$) when written in plain block form. How many of the words NOON, SOS, HEH, ZOZ, NIX, XOX, HOHO look exactly the same after the whole word is turned by a half-turn?
questions.solution: A word survives a half-turn only if every letter is on the list and the word reads the same backwards. NOON, SOS, ZOZ and XOX qualify. HEH contains E, NIX and HOHO are not palindromes, so the answer is 4.

solve.work: NOON, SOS, ZOZ, XOX work; HEH has E, NIX becomes XIN, HOHO becomes OHOH.

questions.stem: A cube with edge 4 is built from 64 unit cubes and stands on a table. From one position a person sees exactly its top face, its front face and its right face. How many of the 64 unit cubes have at least one face that can be seen?
questions.solution: A unit cube is completely hidden if it is not on the top layer, the front layer or the right layer; those hidden cubes form a $3\times3\times3$ block of 27 cubes. So $64-27=37$ cubes have a visible face.

questions.skill: surface area after removing a corner cube
questions.stem: A solid cube has edge 6 cm. A small cube with edge 2 cm is cut away from one corner of it. What is the surface area of the remaining solid, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: Removing the corner takes away three square faces of 4 cm$^2$ from the surface and uncovers three new faces of 4 cm$^2$ at the notch. So the surface area stays $6\times36=216$ cm$^2$.

solve.work: Removing a corner cube exposes 3 faces and removes 3: still 6*36 = 216.

questions.stem: A net of a cube is made of six squares with side 5 cm, joined along whole sides, forming one flat shape without holes. What is the perimeter of the net, in cm?
questions.solution: The six squares have $24$ sides in all. Joining six squares into one piece uses $5$ joins, and each join hides two sides, so $24-10=14$ sides remain on the outline. The perimeter is $14\times5=70$ cm.

questions.stem: A solid has 14 flat faces: 8 triangles and 6 squares. Every edge of the solid is shared by exactly two faces. How many edges does the solid have?
questions.solution: The faces have $8\times3+6\times4=48$ sides in total. Each edge is a side of two faces, so there are $48\div2=24$ edges.

questions.skill: sum of numbers at all vertices of a die
questions.stem: On a standard die, opposite faces add up to 7. At each of the 8 vertices of the die three faces meet; add up the three numbers there. What is the sum of these 8 totals, one for each vertex?
questions.solution: Each face has 4 vertices, so every face number is counted in exactly 4 of the vertex totals. The faces add up to $21$, so the grand total is $4\times21=84$.

questions.stem: A cube is built from $3\times3\times3=27$ unit cubes. The unit cube in the middle of each of the six faces is removed, and so is the unit cube in the very centre of the big cube, leaving 20 unit cubes. What is the surface area of the remaining solid, counting every unit square on the outside and in the holes, in unit squares?
questions.solution: The remaining cubes are the 8 corner cubes and the 12 edge cubes. Each corner cube touches 3 remaining cubes, leaving $6-3=3$ free faces. Each edge cube touches 2 remaining cubes (the corners on its edge), leaving 4 free faces. The total is $8\times3+12\times4=72$.

solve.work: Outside 6*8 = 48 plus 4 inner walls per face hole = 24; check: 20*6 - 2*24 adjacencies = 72.

questions.stem: A large cube, with more than 2 small cubes along each edge, is built from small cubes. Its whole outside is painted and then it is taken apart. The number of small cubes with paint on exactly one face turns out to equal the number of small cubes with no paint at all. How many small cubes are along one edge of the large cube?
questions.solution: With $m$ cubes along an edge, $6(m-2)^2$ have exactly one painted face and $(m-2)^3$ have none. Equal counts give $(m-2)^3=6(m-2)^2$, so $m-2=6$ (as $m>2$) and $m=8$.

questions.skill: sum of edges of a cuboid from volume and area
questions.stem: A cuboid has edges of whole-number lengths in centimetres. Its volume is 30 cm$^3$ and its total surface area is 62 cm$^2$. What is the sum of the lengths of all 12 of its edges, in cm?
questions.solution: Edge triples with product 30 are $1,1,30$; $1,2,15$; $1,3,10$; $1,5,6$; $2,3,5$. Only $2,3,5$ gives surface area $2(6+15+10)=62$. The 12 edges add up to $4\times(2+3+5)=40$ cm.

questions.skill: half-turn symmetric shadings of a grid
questions.stem: The 9 cells of a $3\times3$ grid are in three rows and three columns. Exactly four cells are shaded so that the pattern looks exactly the same after a half-turn ($180^\circ$ rotation) about the centre of the grid. In how many different ways can this be done?
questions.solution: A half-turn swaps cells in pairs (opposite corners, opposite edge cells), except the centre cell, which stays in place. Four shaded cells cannot include the centre, since the other three would not pair up. So we pick 2 of the 4 pairs, which can be done in $\frac{4\times3}{2}=6$ ways.

solve.work: Four rotation pairs plus centre; an even count excludes the centre, so choose 2 pairs: C(4,2) = 6.

questions.skill: surface area of a stack of towers
questions.stem: Unit cubes are stacked on a table in nine columns standing in a $3\times3$ block. Going from front to back there are three rows, each listed from left to right with its heights in cubes. Front row: 3, 1, 2. Middle row: 1, 1, 1. Back row: 2, 1, 3. What is the surface area of the whole solid, including the bottom faces that touch the table, in unit squares?
questions.solution: The tops show 9 unit squares and the bottoms 9 more. For the sides, add along each row (the two ends plus the changes of height): rows give $8+2+8=18$, and along each column likewise $8+2+8=18$. The total is $9+9+18+18=54$.

solve.work: Top+bottom 18, outer sides 6+6+6+6 = 24, inner height differences 3+0+3+3+0+3 = 12; total 54.

questions.stem: A cube with edge 5 is built from 125 unit cubes. Its whole outside surface is painted, and then it is taken apart into the unit cubes. How many unit cubes have an even number of painted faces (zero counts as even)?
questions.solution: No paint: the inner $3\times3\times3$ block gives 27. Exactly two painted faces: cubes on edges but not corners, $12\times3=36$. The total is $27+36=63$. (One face: 54, three faces: 8.)

questions.stem: When a digit is turned by a half-turn ($180^\circ$), let 0, 1 and 8 stay as they are, 6 become 9 and 9 become 6; the other digits do not turn into digits. How many four-digit numbers (from 1000 to 9999) read as the same number after the whole number is turned by a half-turn?
questions.solution: After the half-turn the number reads backwards with each digit turned. So the last digit is the turned first digit, and the third digit is the turned second digit. The first digit is 1, 6, 8 or 9 (not 0): 4 choices. The second digit is 0, 1, 6, 8 or 9: 5 choices. That gives $4\times5=20$ numbers.

solve.work: a = rot(d) with a in {1,6,8,9} (4 ways), b = rot(c) with b in {0,1,6,8,9} (5 ways): 20.

questions.skill: surface area of a cube with two crossing tunnels
questions.stem: A solid cube has edge 10 cm. Two square tunnels, each with a $2\times2$ cm cross-section, are cut through it: one goes straight from the top face to the bottom face, the other straight from the front face to the back face, and both pass through the centre of the cube so that they cross. What is the surface area of the remaining solid, in cm$^2$?
questions.solution: The four openings on the outside remove $4\times4=16$ cm$^2$ from the original 600, leaving 584. Inside, the two walls facing left and right are each plus-shaped: a 2 by 10 strip from each tunnel, overlapping in a 2 by 2 square, so $20+20-4=36$ each, 72 together. Each tunnel also has two other walls, each 2 cm wide and $10-2=8$ cm long because the crossing is open, so $4\times16=64$ in all. The total is $584+72+64=720$ cm$^2$.

solve.work: 600 - 4*4 = 584 outside; tunnel walls 160 minus 8 (vertical front/back cut), 8 (horizontal top/bottom cut), 8 (shared side walls counted twice) = 136; 720.
